transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what’s been going on that brought you in today?

Uh, yeah… I guess the big thing that kind of pushed me to come in is my eating’s been really weird lately. Like, some days I just completely forget to eat, and then other nights I’m up after midnight tearing through takeout or whatever snacks are around.

It sounds small when I say it, but it freaked me out. I work sales, so my schedule’s already kind of all over the place, and you get used to grabbing food whenever, but this feels different. Like I’ll look back and realize I skipped meals without even noticing, then later I’m eating like I haven’t eaten in days.
When you're eating a lot in one sitting, do you feel like you can't stop or control what you're doing?

Yeah… I mean, sometimes it feels like that, kind of. Like I’ll realize I didn’t eat all day, and then it’s midnight and I’m just going through takeout or chips or whatever’s there, and I’m not really thinking about it.

It’s not always like I’m sitting there saying, “I can’t stop,” exactly… it’s more like I don’t notice how much it is until after. Which is weird, because during the day I’ll totally forget meals, like they just don’t register. Sales gets like that sometimes, you know, you’re driving around or making calls and then suddenly it’s night. But this feels more all over the place than normal.
After these times when you've eaten a lot, have you done anything to try to compensate or make up for it, like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or doing extra exercise?

I don’t think so… not like that. I mean, I’ve felt gross after, like too full, and then I’ll tell myself I should eat “better” the next day, but I haven’t been making myself throw up or anything.

Exercise, I mean… I walk around a lot for work sometimes, but that’s not really me trying to burn it off. And laxatives—no, not something I’m doing. Honestly, half the time I’m more annoyed because I spent money on delivery again, like I’ll look at the app and think, “Why did I order from the same place at 1 a.m.?” But yeah, no, I’m not really doing stuff to make up for it.
Do you find yourself feeling guilty, embarrassed, or really hard on yourself after those times when you end up eating a lot?

Yeah… I do. I get pretty hard on myself after, but honestly it kind of turns into this whole thing that’s not even just about the food.

Like I’ll start thinking, “Great, another thing I can’t handle,” and then my brain jumps to work. I keep replaying every mistake I made with those Providence accounts, like over and over, and I start thinking I blew my whole future. Like I’m just useless and everybody at work can see it, you know?

So yeah, embarrassed, guilty… mostly just like I messed everything up somehow.
When you’re eating a lot in one sitting, does it feel like you’re not in control, like you can’t stop eating even if you wanted to?

Yeah… I mean, kind of. It’s not always like I’m thinking, “I can’t stop,” in the moment, but then I’ll look up and I’ve gone through a bunch of takeout and snacks after midnight.

Honestly, that’s kind of the thing that scared me enough to come in. My eating’s been all over the place—some days I forget meals completely, like I’ll just go through the whole day and not even notice, and then other nights it’s like I’m tearing through whatever food I ordered or whatever’s around. It feels weird and out of control, but not in a clean, simple way, if that makes sense.

Can you think of a specific time when you felt like you were eating a lot and not in control? What exactly happened, and did it feel like a distinct episode where you knew, in the moment, that you were losing control?

Yeah… I mean, the closest I can think of is nights after work where I’ll realize I haven’t really eaten all day, and then it’s like after midnight I’m ordering food and just… tearing through it, plus whatever snacks are around.

I don’t know if I’d call it this clear “episode” where I’m sitting there thinking, “I’m losing control.” It’s more like I’m not paying attention, and then suddenly there’s all this food gone and I feel kind of freaked out by it. That’s honestly the part that scared me into coming in—my eating’s just been all over the place. Some days I forget meals completely, and other nights it swings the other way.
When you're eating a lot after not eating all day, does it feel like you're not in control, like you're just going through the motions and can't stop even if you wanted to?

Yeah… sort of. I don’t know if it’s like I’m consciously thinking, “I can’t stop,” but it feels like I’m just on autopilot.

Honestly, the thing that really freaked me out enough to come in is my eating’s been all over the place. Like some days I’ll forget to eat completely, and then other nights it’s after midnight and I’m tearing through takeout and snacks like I’m trying to catch up or something. And then I look at the bags or wrappers and I’m like… what am I doing?
